bundles.name: Identity and designation
bundles.description: Everything needed to tell this individual thing apart from every other thing, to bind marks and identifiers to it, and to decide when it is still the same thing.
bundles.rationale: Instance modelling collapses without a defensible identity rule. Standards agree that instance-level identification is a distinct construct (schema.org IndividualProduct, EPCIS SGTIN/SSCC versus GTIN, ISO/IEC 15459-4 unique identifier for individual items), but they do not agree on scheme, so identity, marking and resolution must be modelled explicitly rather than assumed.

layers.name: Instance identification
layers.description: The identifiers borne by the item, the physical marks and data carriers that carry them, and the resolution of an observed identifier back to one record.

findings.name: Master identifier and issuing authority
findings.description: Which identifier is authoritative for this item, who issued it, under which scheme and syntax, and what uniqueness guarantees apply. ISO/IEC 15459-4 specifies a unique, non-significant string for individual items issued under a registered issuing agency; GS1 expresses the same idea as a primary key plus serial qualifier.

findings.name: Identity marks and data carriers
findings.description: The physical realisation of identity on the thing itself: marking method, placement, durability, legibility, and the machine-readable carrier. IEC 61406-1 requires a globally unique identification link, machine readable via 2D symbol or NFC and attached to the individual unit; ESPR-driven passports require a data carrier on the product.

findings.name: Identifier resolution, aliases and collisions
findings.description: How an observed identifier is resolved to exactly one item record, how multiple scheme identifiers for the same thing are related, and how duplicates, cloned identifiers and merge/split situations are handled.

findings.name: Legibility, cloning risk and distinguishing marks
findings.description: Object ID requires inscriptions and markings, distinguishing features and photographs because unique numbers can be copied, lost or never assigned. A cloned serial or unreadable tag does not by itself prove a second item, nor does it destroy the original item's identity. Condition of the mark is evidence about identification quality, not a new identifier.

findings.name: Digital link, passport and shell
findings.description: IEC 61406-1 defines the IL string as a URL that is both the globally unique identification of a physical object and a pointer to related information. Schema.org requires that a GS1 Digital Link containing serial AI 21 appear only on IndividualProduct. ESPR establishes a digital product passport with a unique product identifier, unique operator identifier and unique facility identifier, accessed via a data carrier on the product. IDTA AAS gives the asset a recommended globalAssetId (IEC 61406 format) and optional specificAssetIds, while the Administration Shell has a separate mandatory id. These are representations and links, not a second physical item.

layers.name: Type linkage and individuation
layers.description: The link from this instance to the class it instantiates, and the rules that decide when the instance begins, persists or ceases to be the same individual.

findings.name: Instance-of-type reference
findings.description: The resolved reference from this individual to its product type or configuration, and the confidence in that resolution. schema.org places IndividualProduct under Product with isVariantOf pointing at a ProductModel; EPCIS keeps class-level identification separate from instance-level identification.

findings.name: Individuation and identity continuity
findings.description: The rules deciding what counts as one item and whether identity survives repair, component replacement, reconfiguration, division or joining. No consulted standard settles this; CIDOC CRM anchors documentation units and composition, and PROV offers specializationOf/alternateOf to relate records without asserting sameness.

findings.name: Configuration and lot inputs
findings.description: A product configuration may classify a configured instance (variant-instance boundary). A lot or batch identifier is not an instance identifier; Schema.org places lot-bearing Digital Links on SomeProducts unless there is only a specific product. IEC 61406-2 separately treats lots/batches. Lot membership and configuration are classification or provenance facts on the instance.

bundles.name: Physical characterisation of the specimen
bundles.description: What is true of this particular specimen as measured or observed, and how it is physically built up, as distinct from what its type specifies.
bundles.rationale: Type models carry nominal specifications; only the instance can carry measured values, as-built content and its own component set. IEC 63278-1 provides a standardized digital representation of an asset across its lifecycle, CIDOC CRM P45 consists of covers material content and P46 is composed of covers parts, and EPCIS aggregation covers physical grouping.

layers.name: Observed and as-built properties
layers.description: Properties measured on this specimen, their measurement context, and the materials it is actually made of.

findings.name: Measured attributes and measurement context
findings.description: Quantities measured on this individual (mass, dimensions, readings) together with unit, method, instrument, uncertainty and the separation of measurement time from record time.

findings.name: Material content and substances of concern
findings.description: What this specimen is actually made of, referenced to material classes rather than restated, including substance declarations that product-passport regimes attach to the individual product.

layers.name: Instance structure and containment boundary
layers.description: The item's membership in assemblies and the point at which instance identity stops and quantity begins.

findings.name: Component membership in an assembly
findings.description: Whether this item is currently or was formerly installed in a parent item, in what position or role, and over what period. The assembly graph itself is mastered by WM-OBJ-012; EPCIS AggregationEvent and CIDOC P46 supply the parent/child semantics.

findings.name: Boundary against quantity, batch and bulk
findings.description: The rule that refuses instance identity to matter with no individuating boundary. ISO 22095 chain-of-custody models such as mass balance and controlled blending explicitly do not preserve one-to-one identity, and EPCIS provides class-level quantity fields precisely for this case.
findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding states a boundary rule and a small set of inline quantity fields. Its outputs are decisions and references into the batch, stock and material sibling models; producing a separate artifact here would duplicate records those models already master.

bundles.name: State, condition and authenticity
bundles.description: Where the item stands in its life, what shape it is in, what has been done to it, and whether it is what it claims to be.
bundles.rationale: EPCIS carries lifecycle meaning in bizStep, disposition and persistentDisposition; ISO 55000 standardises asset life and life-cycle management vocabulary; CIDOC CRM P44 has condition binds condition states to time-spans. Authenticity is separated because a verified mark is an assertion about the identity binding, not about condition.

layers.name: Lifecycle state
layers.description: The item's status in a governed state model and the terminal states that end its tracked existence.

findings.name: Lifecycle status and permitted transitions
findings.description: The current governed status of the item, the transition that produced it, and the constraints on legal transitions. EPCIS disposition expresses the business state of an object after an event, and persistentDisposition expresses states that survive later events.

findings.name: End of life, loss and disposal
findings.description: How the item leaves tracked existence: destruction, recycling, permanent loss, theft or export beyond the record's reach, and what evidence closes the record without deleting it.

findings.name: Loss, theft, seizure, recovery and deaccession
findings.description: Object ID exists because stolen and trafficked objects cannot be recovered without documentation, photographs and distinguishing features; INTERPOL and customs use that documentation. Unknown whereabouts is not the same as non-existence. Seizure, loan, exhibition and deaccession change custody or collection membership without necessarily destroying the object. These states lack a single global code list and must be recorded as explicit exceptional statuses with evidence.

layers.name: Condition and intervention history
layers.description: Dated judgements about the item's physical condition and the record of interventions that changed it.

findings.name: Condition assessment and intervention history
findings.description: Condition as an assessed, dated judgement bound to a scale, assessor and method, together with the repairs, restorations and modifications that altered the individual. CIDOC CRM binds condition states to time-spans; schema.org itemCondition is a commerce enumeration and is not equivalent.

layers.name: Authenticity and verification
layers.description: Whether the physical thing in hand is the thing the record designates.

findings.name: Authenticity verification and cloned-identifier handling
findings.description: Checks that bind the physical thing to the record: mark inspection, carrier verification, tamper evidence and cryptographically verifiable credentials, plus the handling of negative results and duplicate presentations.

bundles.name: Whereabouts and control
bundles.description: Where the item has been observed, what it is inside, who holds it and who owns it.
bundles.rationale: EPCIS separates the read point where an event occurred from the business location where the object is considered to be afterwards; CIDOC CRM separates keeper (P49) from owner (P52); ISO 22095 supplies custody terminology. Conflating observation, containment, custody and title is the most common modelling error in item tracking.

layers.name: Location observation
layers.description: Dated statements of where the item was, with observation quality, and the containers or carriers it was observed within.

findings.name: Location fix and observation quality
findings.description: A dated statement of the item's whereabouts resolved against a place reference, distinguishing the point of observation from the business location asserted afterwards, and carrying precision and source.

findings.name: Containment and carrier context
findings.description: What the item was inside when observed: a handling unit, a vehicle, a room or another item, and how aggregation and disaggregation change that context without changing item identity.

layers.name: Custody, possession and rights
layers.description: Who physically holds the item and under what basis, kept strictly distinct from who owns it.

findings.name: Custody record and transfer
findings.description: Periods during which a named party held the item, the basis of holding, and the transfer events between holders, aligned with ISO 22095 custody terminology and EPCIS source/destination and shipping/receiving semantics.

findings.name: Ownership and rights reference
findings.description: The reference to legal title and encumbrances held in the ownership sibling model, and the rule that possession does not imply title. CIDOC CRM distinguishes current owner (P52) from keeper (P49); ISO 55000 frames value-bearing entities as assets of an organization.

bundles.name: Events, provenance and evidence
bundles.description: The event backbone that produces every other statement about the item, its time semantics, its origin story and the evidence that supports claims.
bundles.rationale: EPCIS models visibility as events answering what, when, where, why and how, with eventTime and recordTime distinguished; PROV-O models generation, derivation and attribution; W3C Verifiable Credentials supply issuer-signed evidence. Together they let claims about an item be traced and challenged rather than merely asserted.

layers.name: Event record and time semantics
layers.description: How events about the item are captured, corrected and ordered in time.

findings.name: Event capture and correction
findings.description: The event structure that records what happened to the item, why, where and how, and the rules for idempotent capture, correction and retraction of events that must not be silently overwritten.

findings.name: Time semantics and ordering
findings.description: The separation of when something happened from when it was recorded, the required timestamp form, and how ordering is decided when clocks disagree. RFC 3339 requires a stated offset to UTC, with 'Z' for zero offset and '-00:00' where the local offset is unknown; EPCIS carries eventTime, eventTimeZoneOffset and repository recordTime separately.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Time semantics govern fields carried by every other finding rather than producing a document of their own. The rules are inline constraints and reference data (offset handling, ordering, precision qualifiers); materialising them as an artifact would duplicate the event stream and the canonicalisation rules already recorded in the service layers.

findings.name: Event dimensions
findings.description: EPCIS 2.0 records What, When, Where, Why and How. Event types are ObjectEvent, AggregationEvent, TransactionEvent, TransformationEvent and AssociationEvent. When includes event time and record time. Why includes bizStep, disposition and persistentDisposition. How includes sensor elements in 2.0. Instance EPCs must not be mixed up with class-level EPCs. Event hash identifiers and business-transaction hash URIs appear in CBV 2.0.

layers.name: Provenance and evidence
layers.description: Where the item came from, through whose hands, and what evidence supports each claim.

findings.name: Origin and chain of custody provenance
findings.description: The origin of the individual (maker, place, date of production or first observation) and the ordered chain of custody from origin to the present, including declared gaps. PROV-O supplies generation, derivation and attribution; ISO 22095 supplies the custody model vocabulary.

findings.name: Attestations, evidence quality and conflicting claims
findings.description: How each claim about the item is supported, who vouches for it, how strong that support is, and what happens when two credible sources disagree.

bundles.name: Record governance and interoperability
bundles.description: Who governs the item record, who may see what, how long it is kept, and how it exchanges with external standards without overclaiming conformance.
bundles.rationale: The record is not the thing. IEC 63278-1 frames a standardized digital representation of an asset across its lifecycle; PROV-O separates entities from the agents responsible for them; GDPR constrains item records that link to identifiable people; product-passport regimes impose external disclosure duties on the economic operator.

layers.name: Record stewardship, access and retention
layers.description: Mastership and authority over the record, scoped disclosure, and privacy and retention duties.

findings.name: Mastership, authority and record lifecycle
findings.description: Which system and which party master this record, who may assert or change each part of it, and how record versions relate to the physical thing they describe.

findings.name: Access scoping and disclosure views
findings.description: Which audiences may see which parts of the record, including a public identity view that deliberately withholds whereabouts and holder, and the exceptions that override the default.

findings.name: Privacy exposure and retention
findings.description: When item data becomes personal data, and how retention duties for traceability are reconciled with data-protection limits. GDPR applies to processing of personal data about identifiable natural persons; item records routinely carry holder identity, ownership history and movement traces.

layers.name: External alignment and exchange
layers.description: How this model maps to external standards and exchanges item data without asserting unproven conformance.

findings.name: Identifier and vocabulary alignment
findings.description: Mappings from this model's terms to external vocabularies (GS1 EPCIS/CBV, GS1 Digital Link, schema.org, IEC 63278-1, CIDOC CRM, PROV-O) recorded as alignments with known conflicts, never as conformance claims.

findings.name: Exchange projections and external obligations
findings.description: The outbound payloads built from this model (visibility events, product-passport content, credential presentations) and the obligations that attach when data is published to an external regime.

model.name: Inventory Stock Position
model.purpose: Describe a source-qualified inventory quantity position by product, ownership, location, status and time.
model.scope_statement: The aggregate owns stock-position identity, declared dimension grain, measured and derived quantities, snapshot currency, reconciliation evidence and bounded operational references. It is informational, not a physical object or execution engine.
in_scope: Stock dimension tuple, custody, restrictions and quantity basis
Reservation and planned-measure semantics with source-defined formulas
Snapshot consistency, count reconciliation, lineage and governed exchange
out_of_scope: Physical product geometry or material remastered as properties of a balance
Inventory booking engine, automatic warehouse actuation and oversell guarantees
Legal title determination, financial valuation and accounting entries

boundary_notes.distinction: REFERENCE only: a stock aggregate is not a serial item or its physical characteristics.
Product identity and unit conversion master stay referenced, not copied.
Movement changes positions but is not itself the current balance; no complete event ledger is assumed.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Reservation, order, warehouse and valuation masters
boundary_notes.distinction: Position retains qualified references and quantities; execution, facility identity and monetary valuation remain external.

functions.name: Read a qualified stock position
functions.description: Retrieve stock for one declared dimension grain.
preconditions: Read permission and source contract
effects: No cross-owner aggregation or missing row interpreted as zero

functions.name: Explain availability
functions.description: Trace source-defined availability formulas without executing reservations.
preconditions: Compatible grain, units and source time
effects: No universal subtraction or physical-stock inference from future reservations

functions.name: Describe projected stock
functions.description: Keep planning-horizon estimates distinct from observed balances.
preconditions: Declared plan version and fulfillment status
effects: No delivery promise or transaction authority granted

functions.name: Reconcile count evidence
functions.description: Compare a count and intervening movement evidence before proposing an adjustment.
preconditions: Matched owner, grain, unit and time
effects: No booking from count alone; approval remains external

functions.name: Route an authorized action
functions.description: Describe a master-mediated reservation or adjustment with explicit uncertain outcomes.
inputs: Expected state and master capability declaration
preconditions: Actual delegated authority and verified endpoint contract
effects: No local property edit masquerades as execution; no blind retry after lost response

functions.name: Exchange with semantic loss report
functions.description: Map authorized stock knowledge while preserving incompatible target constraints.
preconditions: Source disclosure allowed and target constraints checked
effects: Reject unqualified signed stock to positive-only event quantity mapping

composition.purpose: Link identifiable physical items only when item-level evidence exists; aggregate remains nonphysical.
Resolve product identity and qualified unit basis.
Link authoritative stock movements without assuming complete ledger coverage.
Candidate event-evidence alignment with explicit quantity and time mapping losses; not conformance.
Describe attribution and derivation, not permissions or physical truth.

owner_package_requirements: Declare the Dimension owner and delegated inventory steward.
Register authoritative stock, product, movement and location namespaces.
Bind actual read, export, action and retention policies before operation.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Issuer-qualified position ID plus explicit dimension tuple and immutable snapshot ID; neither product code nor timestamp alone identifies the position.

canonicalization_rules: Preserve grain, unit, bucket semantics, effective time and unknown values.
Never add overlapping status buckets or hierarchy reservations without a declared aggregation rule.
patch_rules: Authorized namespaced schema extension with pinned base digest; reject incompatible unit or grain changes.
Corrections append successor snapshots and reasons; stale-base edits do not overwrite a master.
compatibility_rules: A changed bucket meaning or dimension grain needs explicit migration and new schema revision.
Lossy exchange cannot silently replace authoritative stock data.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier
Governed issuer-qualified URI or global identifier
Dimension-issued UUID with issuer context
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; distinguish effective, recorded and counted times. Timestamps are not collision-proof identity.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Artifact-kind prefix plus stable escaped identifier and revision; timestamp may be appended for readability, not uniqueness.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Preserve exact-byte digest, source receipt and mapping version; a digest proves byte identity, not stock truth.

policies: Availability formulas and allowed negative values must be declared by measure and source.
Count evidence does not authorize inventory adjustments or legal ownership changes.
On missing access, incomplete snapshot or stale evidence preserve unknowns; do not infer zero.
Do not retry uncertain operational actions until the authoritative receipt and idempotency capabilities have been checked.

read: Read owner policy, pinned specification, source grain, snapshot currency and access scope before using quantities.
create: Create a qualified snapshot from authorized source evidence; retain unobserved and excluded dimensions explicitly.
update: Append corrected snapshots with expected-base checks and provenance; route operational actions to the authorized master and verify its receipt.
delete: Apply retention and legal-hold policies; tombstone local records with protected provenance, never cascade deletion into product, movement or organization masters.

roles.name: Dimension owner
responsibilities: Defines namespaces and federation policy.

roles.name: Inventory steward
responsibilities: Owns stock measure semantics and source bindings.

roles.name: Count observer
responsibilities: Records evidence without assuming adjustment approval.

roles.name: Adjustment approver
responsibilities: Authorizes a scoped master change under policy.

roles.name: Reviewer
responsibilities: Checks aggregation, reconciliation and mappings.

roles.name: Custodian
responsibilities: Maintains authorized caches and evidence retention.

access.default_rule: Deny unless the owning Dimension explicitly authorizes the scope and purpose.
exceptions: Only recorded scoped and time-limited delegation; no stock custody implies unrestricted disclosure.
audit_requirements: Record actor, purpose, source snapshot, action decision and receipt without secrets.

read_order: Dimension owner and policy
Pinned stock model and source-grain bindings
Authorized snapshot and freshness rules
Dependencies, validation, extensions, action boundaries and retirement

coverage.claim: Proposed stock-position information contract with twelve subject-specific records and thirty-six authored questions. No independent external review, transactional inventory engine or normative conformance is claimed.

checklist.notes: Issuer and complete stock dimension tuple.
Source-qualified stock status and nonphysical aggregate class.
Quantity, unit, precision and declared bucket semantics.
Source keys, dimension grain and observation evidence; not visual item recognition.
Six bounded proposed information operations; execution authority external.
Snapshot correction, count application and action disposition.
Effective, recorded and counted time plus freshness and completeness.
Owner, custodian, product, location, movement and order references.
Snapshot, count and reconstruction evidence.
Goods owner, custodian and data authority distinguished.
Reconciliation, incompatible quantities and incomplete-snapshot fixtures proposed.
Role and owner-scoped disclosure.
Policy-controlled preservation, correction and tombstones.
Source measure mapping with positive-only event quantity limitation.
A quantity position is informational; actual item characteristics remain referenced.
Nested schemas, adapters, real fixtures and independent external review deferred.

known_omissions: Claude and Grok each timed out once. No independent external review; Codex-only result must remain reviewable-draft.
Mutable Microsoft page revision pins remain open; Odoo stock report inspected via indexed text only after direct fetch timeout.
GS1 URL says 2.0.1 while retrieved PDF header says Release 2.0 June 2022; exact normative adapter pin and conformance remain unresolved.
Nested field groups are proposed information contracts, not executable instance schemas; no inventory engine, reservation adapter or concurrency test delivered.
Sector-specific unit conversion, negative-stock, quarantine, consignment and retention profiles need specialist review.
Actual master authority, expected-version and idempotency capabilities must be verified by adopters; source API inspection did not establish these guarantees.
regional_assumptions: Owning Dimension supplies jurisdiction, warehouse, confidentiality and retention policies. No legal ownership or financial valuation determination is made.
adversarial_checks: Reject owner and custodian conflation.
Reject sums across overlapping buckets or reservation hierarchy grains.
Reject absent row, stale value or omitted quantity interpreted as zero.
Reject expected-receipt reservation as physical stock.
Reject a count applied without intervening movement reconciliation.
Reject signed or zero stock blindly exported as positive EPCIS QuantityElement.
Reject local edit treated as execution and uncertain-action blind retries.

providerPolicy.scope: Canonical single-stream subject-model research after the six-workstream consolidation

waived_providers.reason: Claude produced no result on prior 1800-second and 900-second attempts and again timed out on bounded 600-second Sonnet and 300-second Haiku passes. The owner prioritized completion over provider availability.

The repository owner authorized completion without Grok when Grok is unavailable, slow or schema-invalid. Grok may still be attempted as a bounded supplemental reviewer, but its failure never blocks a valid Claude plus no-tools result.

providerPolicy.review_rule: Codex may complete source-grounded fallback research after bounded Claude and Grok attempts fail. It requires a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remains reviewable-draft with a visible absence-of-external-review hold.

supplemental_provider_attempts.admission_rule: Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.
Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.

boundaryDecision.rationale: A source-qualified stock position aggregates quantities at a declared grain and time. Physical item, product, location, movement, reservation and valuation masters remain distinct; frozen REFERENCE WM-OBJ-001 is preserved.

decisions.rationale: Quantity and stock grain are intrinsic; geometry and material belong to referenced physical subjects.
Source-defined hierarchy, overlap and offsets prevent naive totals; custody is not ownership and expected receipts are not on-hand.
Snapshots expose consistency and freshness; counts need reconciliation before authorized application; action effects require actual master receipts.
Evidence alignment does not imply balance reconstruction; signed and zero balances require explicit target constraint handling.
Selected source passages motivate candidate contracts; revision pins, nested schemas, adapters and real concurrency fixtures are not established.
One terminal timeout per external provider; frozen no-tools Codex self-review is not independent evidence.

publicationHolds: No independent external research or review: Claude and Grok each timed out once. Codex-only research and self-audit remain reviewable-draft, never canonical.
Mutable Microsoft revision pins remain open. Odoo stock-report evidence is selected indexed text; its direct fetch timed out.
GS1 URL 2.0.1 returned a PDF labelled Release 2.0 June 2022. Exact normative adapter version and conformance remain unresolved.
No executable nested instance schema, transactional inventory engine, reservation adapter, concurrency fixture or verified round-trip translation is delivered.
Warehouse and sector-specific conversion, quarantine, consignment, negative-stock and retention policies need specialist review.
Adopters must verify real master permissions, snapshot consistency, expected-version and idempotency capabilities before operational use.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Independent external review and exact source revision pins.
Executable typed fields and negative fixtures for overlapping status and reservation hierarchies.
Concurrent counting, uncertain-action receipts and complete snapshot tests against actual inventory masters.
Loss-aware EPCIS and inventory API adapters with signed and unknown quantity fixtures.

model.name: Goods Movement / Logistics
model.purpose: Represent the governed plan and observed history of moving identified physical goods through routes, legs, custody transitions, milestones and exceptions independently of storage, interface or transport provider.
model.scope_statement: Owns movement, shipment and consignment identity and boundary, cargo and handling-unit bindings, routes, multimodal legs, schedules, observations, derived status, custody assertions, condition bindings, exceptions, ETA, replanning, regulatory-status references, projections and standards mappings while neighboring masters own physical objects and legal or commercial lifecycles.
in_scope: Movement, shipment and consignment identities, party roles, service constraints, cargo lines, package and handling-unit composition and equipment bindings
Origins, destinations, routes, ordered multimodal legs, planned and actual milestones, custody assertions, condition evidence, exceptions, ETA, replanning and delivery outcomes
Regulatory status references, identifier reconciliation, provenance, access, retention, stakeholder projections and interoperability crosswalks
out_of_scope: Sale, order, title, ownership, inventory accounting, financial valuation, contract, procurement, invoice, payment, insurance claim or customs-declaration master lifecycles
Goods, lot, product, package, handling unit, transport equipment, vehicle, vessel, aircraft, facility, location, party, organization, sensor, evidence or document master lifecycles
Universal mode-specific operations, routing algorithms, tariff rules, dangerous-goods law, sanctions, customs clearance logic, carrier liability or proof-of-delivery law

boundary_notes.neighbor: Goods, Product, Lot, Package and Handling Unit
boundary_notes.distinction: The movement binds identified cargo and versions containment or aggregation for transport, while physical and commercial object properties remain externally mastered.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Vehicle, Vessel, Aircraft and Transport Equipment
boundary_notes.distinction: A leg references the means and equipment performing or containing movement; their registration, capacity, maintenance, location and lifecycle stay external.
Parties and places are assigned interval-specific logistics roles and functions but retain authoritative identity and lifecycle in their masters.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Order, Contract, Invoice, Payment, Ownership and Inventory
boundary_notes.distinction: Commercial, legal, financial and stock records may motivate or evidence movement but are not movement events and remain typed references.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Customs, Permit, Sanction and Regulatory Decision
boundary_notes.distinction: The model binds authoritative declarations, holds, releases and permissions plus their operational effect without reproducing border-agency decision lifecycles.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Sensor, Observation, Evidence, Incident and Claim
boundary_notes.distinction: Condition streams, proof, generic incidents and legal or insurance claims retain their master records; movement stores scoped observations, summaries and resolvable links.

preconditions: locations, modes and dependencies resolve

effects: derived state may change under deterministic precedence

preconditions: correction authority and evidence resolve

functions.name: Record custody handover

owner_package_requirements: Declare the Dimension owner, movement steward, shipper, carrier and handling authorities, party and goods masters, regulatory interfaces, evidence custodian and disclosure authority.
Declare shipment, consignment, goods, package, handling-unit, equipment, vehicle, facility, route, contract, customs, sensor, document and party master systems.
Publish model, object, event, relation, identifier, location, access, retention, assurance and interoperability registries.

dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint movement, shipment, consignment, route, leg, observation, exception and revision identifiers only in the adopting Dimension's governed namespace; preserve goods, handling-unit, equipment, vehicle, party, facility, contract, customs, sensor and document identifiers as typed external references with authority, version and time.
registry_links: Dimension-local movement, shipment, location, identifier, event, access and provenance registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by registry ID, model version, authoritative logistics master ID, immutable revision, object class, scope and issuer; never use tracking number, status, place, timestamp, filename or hash alone as identity.

Keep movement, shipment, consignment, booking, cargo item, package, handling unit, equipment, route, leg, observation, custody assertion and regulatory record distinct and preserve corrections and supersession.
patch_rules: Additive extensions use a Dimension-owned namespace and declare target node, mode or cargo profile, authority, source, rationale, access, event and interoperability impact.
Breaking changes require a new version, migration and crosswalk maps, compatibility declaration and continued resolution of prior plans, events and external identifiers.
compatibility_rules: Consumers may ignore unknown additive fields only when movement identity, object class, scope, place, time kind, state, authority, provenance and access meaning remain intact.
UN/CEFACT, EPCIS, CBV, DCSA, ONE Record, WCO and IMO mappings pin source and target versions and declare transformed, omitted or non-round-trippable values.

identity_priority: Authoritative logistics master-system identifier and immutable revision identifier.
Governed globally resolvable movement, consignment, leg or event IRI.
Adopting-Dimension UUID or ULID when no authoritative external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record event timestamps in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z; keep requested, planned, estimated, predicted, actual, sensor, capture, record, correction and ingestion times distinct.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Name serial artifacts as {movement-id}--{artifact-kind}--{revision-or-event-id}; never use a tracking number, status, place, date, filename or hash alone as movement identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, byte length, issuer, source and vocabulary versions, object scope, event and record times, provenance, assurance and access marking for every retained serial artifact.

policies: The adopting Dimension declares who may plan, book, bind cargo, observe, hand over, correct, replan, classify exceptions, bind regulatory status, disclose, retain and tombstone logistics records.

Every movement assertion requires subject class and identity, cargo or equipment scope, leg or route context, place, time kind, source, authority, confidence, status and revision lineage as applicable.
Agents never infer physical occurrence, custody, title, ownership, delivery acceptance, customs clearance, compliance or claim liability from a plan, estimate, scan or status code alone.

Goods, handling units, equipment, vehicles, parties, facilities, contracts, customs records, permits, invoices, payments, sensor streams, evidence and documents remain in their owning systems and are referenced.

Automated agents may append low-risk observations, predictions, reconciliations and projections under delegation, but custody acceptance, route changes with material risk, regulatory action, consequential disclosure and irreversible deletion default to confirmation or accountable authority.

read: Resolve active Dimension, purpose, role, movement profile, object scope, time horizon, requested revision, assurance, freshness and access policy; return the minimum permitted projection.
create: Create stable movement identity, class, scope, parties, cargo references, origin, destination, period, source, authority and explicit unknowns before planning or observation.
update: Append an immutable plan, event or assertion revision with actor, authority, reason, RFC 3339 effective time and predecessor; validate identifiers, containment, route, time, evidence and access before and after mutation.
delete: Apply carriage, customs, insurance, dispute, audit, retention and legal-hold policy; tombstone eligible records or withdraw projections while preserving identity, material observations and non-cascading external references.

coverage.claim: A source-grounded reviewable draft of Goods Movement / Logistics across UN/CEFACT, UN/LOCODE, GS1 EPCIS and CBV, DCSA, IATA ONE Record, WCO, IMO, W3C provenance and IETF time standards, without a claim of universal mode, jurisdiction, dangerous-goods, customs or legal-proof completeness.

checklist.notes: Movement, shipment, consignment, booking, cargo line, package, handling unit, equipment, route, leg, event, exception and revision identities are distinct.
Object class, mode, role, event type, business step, disposition, exception, condition and regulatory profile are versioned.
The informational movement object's scope, status, route, schedule, cargo bindings and constraints are covered; physical properties of goods, equipment and vehicles remain in their masters.
Agents distinguish plan, estimate, actual observation, correction, custody assertion and external authority decision by type, source, actor, time and evidence.
Registration, planning, booking reference, pickup, movement, transfer, delivery, return, exception, correction, replanning, closure and tombstone preserve history.
Cargo, packages, units, equipment, legs, locations, parties, custody intervals, contracts, customs records, sensors and evidence use typed bindings.
Requested, planned, cut-off, estimated, predicted, actual, sensor, capture, record, correction and ingestion times remain distinct.
Origins, destinations, waypoints, facilities, read points, business locations, coordinates, functions, corridors and uncertainty are explicit.
Sources, actors, activities, methods, observations, corrections, estimates, evidence snapshots and successor revisions are linked.
Dimension owner, movement steward, carrier, handler, object steward, regulator, reviewer and disclosure authority have separate responsibilities.
Identity, containment, quantity, unit, route order, time, event precedence, custody, condition, regulatory and crosswalk checks are explicit.
Role, purpose, delegation, field-level controls, live-location sensitivity, redaction, emergency access and audit are represented.
Immutable observations, corrections, custody and regulatory evidence, retention, legal hold, withdrawal and tombstones are explicit.
UN/CEFACT, UN/LOCODE, EPCIS, CBV, DCSA, ONE Record, WCO and IMO profiles pin versions and disclose loss.

Registration, cargo binding, route planning, observation, correction, handover, condition capture, ETA, exception, regulatory binding, reconciliation and projection functions declare controlled effects.

known_omissions: Mode, jurisdiction, dangerous-goods, customs, carriage, liability, insurance, sanctions, privacy and retention profiles require exact current rules and competent review.
Goods, product, lot, package, handling-unit, equipment, vehicle, facility, party, contract, customs, invoice, payment, sensor, evidence and claim lifecycles remain in neighboring masters.
Certified field-level crosswalks, carrier-specific code mappings, routing algorithms, ETA validation suites and legal proof requirements remain future work.
conflicts: Shipment, consignment and transport movement overlap across standards; this aggregate preserves typed local concepts and requires explicit crosswalks rather than choosing one vocabulary as universal.
EPCIS and carrier tracking events are observations with business context, not automatic proof of custody, title, ownership, delivery acceptance or regulatory compliance.
Generic logistics must support multiple modes while mode-specific operational, safety and regulatory semantics remain governed profiles and references.
regional_assumptions: WCO and IMO sources define cross-border and maritime profiles, not universal requirements for domestic or non-maritime movement.
DCSA Track and Trace 2.2 specializes container shipping and IATA ONE Record 3.2.0 specializes air cargo; neither is treated as the generic ontology alone.
UN/LOCODE release content changes under an official maintenance process, so adopting Dimensions must retain directory version and status.
adversarial_checks: Reject merging shipment, consignment, booking, cargo item, package, handling unit and transport equipment solely because one provider uses a shared identifier.
Reject actual movement, custody, delivery acceptance, clearance or compliance inferred only from a plan, ETA, scan, status label or API response.
Reject last-write-wins when carrier events conflict; preserve source, event time, record time, correction lineage, confidence and deterministic precedence.
Reject an ETA or route change that overwrites actual events or the prior plan or omits model, input cut-off, confidence, authority and successor rationale.
Reject copying goods, vehicle, facility, customs, contract, payment, sensor or claim lifecycles into the movement record when authoritative typed references suffice.

boundaryDecision.status: accepted with typed logistics objects and profiles
boundaryDecision.rationale: Movement, shipment, consignment, cargo composition, route, leg, observation, custody assertion and exception form one operational context aggregate, while physical, commercial, regulatory, sensor and evidentiary masters remain external references.

decisions.rationale: Standards overlap in terminology, so the model records class, authority and mapping instead of treating carrier identifiers as universal synonyms.

decisions.concept: Cargo, package, handling unit and equipment
decisions.rationale: Transport aggregation may change without changing the goods, and equipment contains handling units without becoming their product identity.
Goods, lots, packages, equipment, vehicles, facilities and sensors retain their direct physical properties and lifecycle outside the movement aggregate.
Requested, planned, estimated, predicted, actual, corrected, record and ingestion times cannot overwrite or substitute for one another.
Status derives from append-only observations, authority, time and deterministic precedence rather than last-write-wins.
Possession, operational control, carrier responsibility, custody, stewardship, title and ownership may differ by object and interval.
A scan or EPCIS-style event is an observation with business context and is not automatic proof of physical occurrence, custody, delivery acceptance or compliance.

decisions.disposition: accepted as versioned predictions and successor plans
decisions.rationale: Predictions retain model, inputs, cut-off, confidence and override provenance, and replanning preserves original intent and actual history.
The movement records operational consequences of holds, releases, permits and certificates while border authorities own their decisions and lifecycle.
DCSA and IATA specialize ocean-container and air-cargo exchange while the base remains mode-neutral and uses pinned mappings.
Cargo, party, value, route, condition and current-location detail can be commercially, personally or operationally sensitive and requires purpose-bound field access.

The structure covers identity, composition, planning, observation, custody, condition, exceptions, actions, regulatory interfaces, validation, provenance, access, retention and interoperability, but specialist profiles still require review.

Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.

model.name: Shipment / Consignment
model.purpose: Represent one governed trade shipment or transport consignment, or an explicitly combined logistics view, with goods scope, parties, endpoints, many-to-many allocation, requirements, status assertions and correction lineage without becoming its goods, movement, handling units, documents, trace or fulfilment obligation.
model.scope_statement: Owns mandatory shipment-or-consignment semantic kind; object and revision identity; commercial, carrier, customs and party identifiers; trade and transport party-role bindings; shipment-consignment allocation; item, quantity, value and origin bindings; package, handling-unit and equipment membership references; logistics locations and movement-plan references; service, handling, dangerous-goods, temperature, security, customs and regulatory requirements; planned, estimated, predicted, observed and actual milestone assertions; shipment-scoped custody and responsibility bindings; exceptions and outcome references; qualified measures; document and evidence references; provenance, reconciliation, access, retention and loss-aware projections. Goods, products, orders, contracts, fulfilment, handling units, inventory movements, journeys, routes, services, schedules, parties, places, bookings, transport documents, customs declarations, dangerous-goods masters, sensors, generic events, chain of custody, incidents, insurance claims and evidence masters remain external.
in_scope: Shipment or consignment identity, revision, mandatory semantic kind, party and endpoint boundary, many-to-many allocation and successor lineage
Goods-item scope, package and handling-unit membership references, requirements, movement bindings, milestone assertions, qualified measures and documents
Status, exceptions, responsibility bindings, provenance, reconciliation, privacy, access, retention and interoperability
out_of_scope: Owning goods, products, orders, contracts, fulfilment, handling units, inventory movement, journey, route, service, schedule, party, place, booking, document, declaration, dangerous-goods master, sensor, trace, incident, claim, evidence or payment lifecycles

Equating shipment with consignment, item with package, package with handling unit, custody with ownership, transport status with inventory state, plan with actual movement, milestone assertion with trace event or proof of delivery with fulfilment

Performing transportation, inventory mutation, customs clearance, dangerous-goods certification, custody proof, claims determination, autonomous consequential rerouting, protected disclosure or irreversible deletion

boundary_notes.distinction: Goods Movement / Logistics is a broader flow context. Shipment / Consignment owns the bounded trade or transport grouping and its assertions; the registered parent signal remains candidate until both models are jointly reviewed.

Shipment / Consignment records membership, loading, marks and seals. Handling-unit identity, physical properties, nesting, condition and lifecycle remain externally mastered; CONTAINS is accepted only as typed membership.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-FLW-009 Journey / Trip and WM-FLW-010 Route / Itinerary
boundary_notes.distinction: Shipment / Consignment binds planned or actual transport references and milestones. Journey execution, route geometry, movement observations and outcomes remain externally mastered.
A shipment milestone may cause or correlate with inventory movement, but stock ledger, location balance, reservation and inventory adjustment remain Inventory Movement concerns.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-FLW-013 Supply-chain Trace / Chain of Custody
boundary_notes.distinction: The model binds source-qualified milestones and current custody or responsibility assertions. Cross-organizational event graph, chain-of-custody proof and trace-query lifecycle remain in the trace pattern.
Fulfilment may reference shipments as physical delivery evidence. Commercial obligation, acceptance, proof evaluation, remedies and fulfilment outcome remain externally mastered.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Transport document, Customs declaration and Insurance claim
boundary_notes.distinction: Shipping instructions, waybills, bills of lading, declarations and claims are independently governed records referenced by the shipment or consignment; their issuance, legal effect and adjudication are external.

dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint shipment, consignment, revision, allocation, item-binding, milestone-assertion, exception and projection identifiers only in the adopting Dimension namespace; preserve external master identities as typed references.

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by registry ID, model version, mandatory semantic kind, authoritative master ID, immutable revision, party and endpoint boundary, item scope and source profile; never use date, tracking number, document number, barcode, endpoint pair or hash alone as identity.

Keep trade shipment, transport consignment, goods item, consignment item, package, handling unit, transport equipment, inventory movement, journey, trace event, delivery obligation and transport document distinct and preserve allocations, corrections and successors.
patch_rules: Additive extensions use a Dimension-owned namespace and declare target node, trade, mode or jurisdiction profile, authority, source, rationale, access, time and interoperability impact.
Breaking changes require a new version, migration and crosswalk maps, compatibility declaration and continued resolution of prior object revisions, allocations and identifiers.
compatibility_rules: Consumers may ignore unknown additive fields only when kind, identity, item allocation, parties, endpoints, clocks, status, authority, provenance and access meaning remain intact.
UN/CEFACT, WCO, UBL, GS1, IATA, DCSA, eFTI, UN/LOCODE, units and provenance mappings pin source and target versions and declare transformed, omitted or non-round-trippable values.

identity_priority: Authoritative shipment or consignment master-system identifier and immutable revision.
Governed globally resolvable shipment, consignment, allocation or milestone IRI.
Adopting-Dimension UUID or ULID when no authoritative external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record event timestamps in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z; keep planned, estimated, predicted, observed, actual, record, correction and ingestion times distinct.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Name serial artifacts as {shipment-or-consignment-id}--{artifact-kind}--{revision-or-event-id}; never use a date, tracking code, document number, barcode, party, location, filename or hash alone as identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, byte length, issuer, source and vocabulary versions, object scope, event and record times, provenance, assurance, license and access marking for each retained serial artifact.

policies: The adopting Dimension declares who may create, allocate, compose, bind, instruct, assert status, correct, disclose, retain and tombstone shipment or consignment records.

Every assertion requires mandatory semantic kind, identity and revision, item or logistics scope, party and endpoint context, time kind, source, authority, confidence, status and lineage as applicable.

Agents never infer ownership, custody, fulfilment, inventory state, legal permission, customs clearance, safe handling, delivery completion or claim validity from a status, tracking code, document or location alone.

Goods, orders, fulfilment, handling units, inventory movements, journeys, routes, services, parties, locations, contracts, bookings, documents, declarations, dangerous-goods masters, sensors, trace, incidents, claims and evidence remain external masters.

Automated agents may append low-risk memberships, status assertions, reconciliations and projections under delegation, but custody transfer, customs declaration, dangerous-goods decisions, protected disclosure and irreversible deletion require accountable authority.

read: Resolve active Dimension, purpose, role, mandatory kind, requested revision, item scope, status horizon, assurance, freshness, license and access policy; return the minimum permitted projection.
create: Create stable identity, mandatory kind, party and endpoint boundary, item scope, source, authority and explicit unknowns before adding allocations, units or milestone assertions.
update: Append an immutable allocation, composition, instruction, status, measurement, exception or correction revision with actor, authority, reason, RFC 3339 effective time and predecessor.
delete: Apply trade, customs, safety, dispute, audit, retention, disposition and legal-hold policy; tombstone eligible Shipment / Consignment-owned records or withdraw projections while preserving identity, material provenance and non-cascading external references. The adopting Dimension policy owns execution.

access.default_rule: Deny mutation and sensitive disclosure unless the active Dimension, role, purpose, object kind, trade confidentiality, location sensitivity, customs or safety rule, license and field policy grant the action; expose the minimum necessary projection.
exceptions: Emergency or regulatory access must be legally grounded, time-limited, purpose-bound, attributable, independently reviewed and unable to erase immutable shipment, consignment, correction or legal-hold evidence.
audit_requirements: Log actor, role, purpose, object and revision identity, action, decision, policy and vocabulary versions, RFC 3339 timestamp with offset, affected fields, source evidence and outcome for privileged mutation or disclosure.

read_order: Read the nearest Dimension-owner AGENTS.md, trade and transport authority, active mode, jurisdiction, time, access, retention, licensing and disclosure policies.

Read this model AGENTS.md, pinned spec.yaml and required goods, order, handling-unit, inventory, journey, route, service, party, location, contract, booking, document, declaration, dangerous-goods, trace, sensor, incident, claim and evidence model instructions before mutation.

coverage.claim: WM-FLW-011 covers a governed Shipment / Consignment aggregate family with a mandatory semantic kind, shipment-consignment many-to-many allocation, goods and package composition, handling-unit membership, locations and movement references, service and compliance requirements, milestone assertions, responsibility, exceptions, measures, documents, provenance, access and loss-aware projections. Trade, mode, jurisdiction, dangerous-goods, customs, implementation-conformance and independent-review questions remain deferred.

checklist.notes: Trade shipment, transport consignment, revision, allocation, item binding, milestone assertion and projection identities remain distinct.
Mandatory kind separates seller-to-buyer goods grouping from consignor-to-consignee transport-contract grouping.
Party and endpoint boundary, item scope, requirements, qualified measures and status assertions are covered without importing external masters.
Master assertion, plan, prediction, status report, EPCIS event, sensor observation, document and correction are distinguished.
Draft, planned, booked, accepted, picked-up, in-transit, arrived, delivered, returned, cancelled, corrected and tombstoned states preserve history.
Trade and transport parties, goods, packages, handling units, journeys, routes, services, documents, declarations, trace and claims use typed bindings.
Planned, estimated, predicted, observed, actual, record, correction and ingestion clocks remain distinct.
Origin, destination, receipt, loading, transshipment, unloading, border, storage and delivery location functions are explicit.
Sources, actors, methods, documents, events, derivations, revisions and invalidations are linked.
Trade ownership, custody, possession, control, risk, responsibility and data mastership are not conflated.
Identity, kind, many-to-many allocation, quantity balance, membership, endpoint, clock, requirement, measurement, document and crosswalk checks are explicit.
Role, purpose, commercial confidentiality, customs, safety, location sensitivity, minimum projection and audit are represented.
Corrections, disputes, customs or legal hold, withdrawal and tombstones are explicit and non-cascading.
UN/CEFACT, WCO, UBL, GS1, IATA, DCSA, eFTI, UN/LOCODE, ISO, RFC, PROV, DQV and ODRL mappings disclose loss.
Registration, allocation, item composition, unit binding, movement binding, requirements, milestones, exceptions, reconciliation and projection declare controlled effects.

known_omissions: Trade, mode, region, customs, dangerous-goods, security, temperature, food, pharmaceutical, animal, waste, sanctions, export-control, safety, privacy, licensing and retention profiles require exact current rules and competent review.

Goods, orders, contracts, fulfilment, handling units, inventory, journeys, routes, services, bookings, documents, declarations, dangerous-goods masters, trace, sensors, incidents, claims and evidence lifecycles remain in neighboring models.
Certified field crosswalks, status inference, ETA, exception causality, custody proof, customs admissibility and legal evidence requirements remain future work.
conflicts: UN/CEFACT and WCO use shipment as the trade or goods view and consignment as the transport-contract view, while UBL describes them as contractual or logical versus physical or logistical views; the model requires a mandatory semantic kind and source profile.
Shipment and consignment have many-to-many allocation under split and consolidated transport, so neither can be treated as the universal container of the other.

A tracking status, EPCIS event, sensor reading, transport document, customs declaration and proof of delivery are different assertion or evidence classes and cannot silently establish ownership, custody, fulfilment or legal clearance.
regional_assumptions: WCO customs guidance and EU eFTI rules are regulatory profiles rather than universal commercial or transport law.
IATA ONE Record and DCSA Track and Trace are modal profiles for air cargo and container shipping and do not define all shipment types.
Dangerous-goods, customs, sanctions, transport documents, title, custody and delivery consequences depend on mode, contract and jurisdiction.
adversarial_checks: Reject an object without stable identity, mandatory shipment-or-consignment kind, revision, party and endpoint boundary, item scope, source and lineage.
Reject shipment and consignment collapsed into one identity or a one-to-many-only relationship that cannot represent split and consolidated transport.
Reject a goods item, package, handling unit, container, inventory movement, journey, status event, document or delivery obligation represented as the shipment or consignment itself.
Reject planned, estimated, predicted, observed and actual milestone times collapsed into one timestamp or interpreted without source and timezone rules.
Reject custody, ownership, fulfilment, customs clearance, safe condition or delivery inferred from location, tracking status, waybill or proof label alone.
Reject last-write-wins when item quantities, handling-unit membership, status assertions, measurements or documents conflict; preserve source, clocks, correction and precedence.
Reject protected commercial or location disclosure, dangerous-goods decision, customs submission or record destruction outside delegated authority.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Cross-domain discovery justifies one aggregate family only when every instance declares trade-shipment, transport-consignment or combined-logistics-view. Goods, obligations, handling units, inventory, movement, trace, documents, declarations, claims and evidence remain external masters.

decisions.rationale: Trade shipment and transport consignment are related views but have different party, contract and allocation semantics.
UN/CEFACT and WCO separate what goods are shipped from how they move under a transport contract.
One shipment may use several consignments and one consignment may consolidate all or part of several shipments.
Goods Movement / Logistics is broader, and the relation ledger does not yet approve inheritance.
Shipment or consignment can group handling units, while unit identity, physical state, nesting and lifecycle remain external.
Shipment / Consignment binds movement journeys and milestones but does not own movement execution or observations.
Stock mutation and cross-organizational chain-of-custody event graphs remain in WM-FLW-012 and WM-FLW-013.
Tracking status, EPCIS events, sensor observations and predicted milestones cannot silently overwrite master assertions.
Instructions, waybills, bills of lading, customs declarations and certificates retain independent identity, issuance and legal effect.
UN/CEFACT, WCO, UBL, GS1, IATA, DCSA and eFTI use different scopes, profiles and legal contexts.

decisions.concept: Single-provider waiver and local no-tools audit
decisions.rationale: One bounded Claude Sonnet and one bounded Grok attempt each timed out after 120 seconds. Codex separately audited the frozen validated result and comparison without acquiring new facts, so assurance remains reviewable-draft.

publicationHolds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok attempt for WM-FLW-011 each timed out after 120 seconds; no external result was admitted.
Aggregate hold: every instance must declare trade-shipment, transport-consignment or combined-logistics-view.
Relation hold: WM-FLW-004 remains a compositional reference rather than an approved parent until joint boundary review.
Containment hold: WM-OBJ-021 is a typed membership target; handling-unit identity, physical state, nesting and lifecycle remain external.
Boundary hold: goods, orders, fulfilment, inventory movement, journey execution, trace, documents, declarations, claims and evidence remain external masters.
Terminology hold: shipment, consignment, goods shipment, trade shipment, cargo, item, piece, package, handling unit and transport equipment are profile-specific terms.
Mode hold: air, road, rail, maritime, inland-waterway, postal, courier, multimodal and autonomous-freight profiles need independent validation.
Jurisdiction hold: customs, dangerous-goods, sanctions, export control, security, temperature, title, custody, privacy, licensing and retention rules depend on context.
Evidence hold: tracking status, document possession, a location event or proof label does not alone prove ownership, custody, fulfilment, safe condition or legal clearance.
Interoperability hold: every UN/CEFACT, WCO, UBL, GS1, IATA, DCSA, eFTI, UN/LOCODE, ISO, RFC, PROV, DQV and ODRL projection needs exact pins, conformance evidence and semantic-loss declarations.
Review hold: trade, transport, customs, dangerous-goods, safety, privacy, logistics, data governance, records and independent external review are outstanding.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Approve or reject the WM-FLW-004 parent relation after joint Goods Movement / Logistics boundary review.
Create independently validated trade-shipment, transport-consignment, air-cargo, ocean-container, road, rail, parcel, cold-chain, dangerous-goods, humanitarian and waste profiles.
Benchmark identifier matching, split and consolidation allocation, quantity reconciliation, status inference, ETA, exception causality, custody proof and customs admissibility.
Pin exact releases and licensing conditions and obtain independent domain review before promotion beyond reviewable-draft assurance.

model.name: Inventory Movement
model.purpose: Represent one governed stock-affecting movement assertion, its subject, quantity, source-destination transition, execution and posting references, evidence and correction lineage without becoming the inventory position, ledger, product, location, task or shipment.
model.scope_statement: Owns movement identity and revision; assertion kind, class, direction and reason; idempotency and correction lineage; item, lot, serial and handling-unit scope references; qualified quantity; source and destination position, location, owner, custodian, status and disposition references; request, order, reservation, task, production and shipment triggers; lifecycle and clocks; execution observations; external authoritative posting references; exceptions, reconciliation, provenance, access, retention and loss-aware projections. Product, lot, serial, handling unit, location, stock position and balance, order, warehouse task, production, shipment, journey, chain of custody, ledger, valuation, accounting, document, observation, incident and evidence masters remain external.
in_scope: Movement identity, class, assertion kind, revision, idempotency, direction, reason and successor lineage
Stock-subject scope, qualified quantity, source-destination and stock-bucket transition references, triggers, execution and posting assertions
Lifecycle clocks, evidence, exceptions, reconciliation, governance, access, retention and interoperability
out_of_scope: Owning product, material, lot, serial, handling unit, place, inventory position, stock balance, order, reservation, task, production, shipment, journey, trace, ledger, valuation, accounting, document, observation, incident or evidence lifecycles

Equating request with execution, physical movement with posting, custody with ownership, location with stock status, position with movement, count discrepancy with adjustment or shipment milestone with inventory receipt
Executing warehouse operations, inventory ledger mutation, accounting posting, autonomous physical handling, safety decisions, protected disclosure or irreversible deletion

boundary_notes.distinction: Inventory Movement references before-and-after positions and may support an externally calculated balance change. Position identity, balance computation and snapshot lifecycle remain external; the candidate parent signal is held for review.
A shipment groups goods and logistics obligations. Inventory Movement owns a stock-affecting transition that may be triggered or evidenced by despatch or receipt but does not own the shipment.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-FLW-013 Supply-chain Trace / Chain of Custody
boundary_notes.distinction: Inventory Movement owns one movement assertion and its correction lineage. Cross-organizational critical-event graphs and custody proof remain externally mastered.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Product, lot, serial and handling unit
boundary_notes.distinction: The movement binds subject identities and aggregation scope. Their descriptive properties, composition, condition and independent lifecycles remain external.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Order, reservation, warehouse task and production
boundary_notes.distinction: These objects trigger or authorize planned work. Inventory Movement records their references and observed effects but not their workflow or resource scheduling.
The model records external posting identity, authority, time and result reference. It does not calculate balances, cost inventory or create accounting entries.
Scans, counts, sensor readings, receipt or despatch documents and incident records are independently governed evidence references, not the movement identity or automatic master truth.

dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint movement, revision, transition, execution-assertion, posting-reference, reconciliation and projection identifiers only in the adopting Dimension namespace; preserve external identities as typed references.
registry_links: Dimension-local movement, stock-status, location, unit, posting, access, retention and provenance registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by registry ID, model version, authoritative movement ID, immutable revision, assertion kind, stock-subject scope, source-destination transition and source profile; never use date, document number, barcode, quantity, endpoint pair or hash alone as identity.
Keep request, plan, reservation, physical execution, observation, posting, resulting stock position, correction and reconciliation distinct and preserve causal links.
patch_rules: Additive extensions use a Dimension-owned namespace and declare target node, movement or industry profile, authority, source, rationale, access, time and interoperability impact.
Breaking changes require a new version, migration and crosswalk maps, compatibility declaration and continued resolution of prior movement revisions, postings and identifiers.
compatibility_rules: Consumers may ignore unknown additive fields only when identity, assertion kind, stock subject, quantity, transition, clocks, authority, provenance and access meaning remain intact.
GS1, UBL, UN/CEFACT, ISA-95, IEC 62264, units and provenance mappings pin source and target versions and declare transformed, omitted or non-round-trippable values.

identity_priority: Authoritative inventory or warehouse master-system movement identifier and immutable revision.
Governed globally resolvable movement, transition, posting or reconciliation IRI.
Adopting-Dimension UUID or ULID when no authoritative external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record timestamps in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z; keep planned, effective, event, observation, record, posting, correction and ingestion times distinct.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Name serial artifacts as {movement-id}--{artifact-kind}--{revision-or-event-id}; never use a date, document number, barcode, quantity, location, filename or hash alone as identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, byte length, issuer, source and vocabulary versions, subject and transition scope, event and record times, provenance, assurance, license and access marking for each retained serial artifact.

policies: The adopting Dimension declares who may request, plan, reserve, execute, observe, post, approve, reverse, correct, reconcile, disclose, retain and tombstone inventory movements.

Every assertion requires movement identity and revision, assertion kind, stock subject, qualified quantity, transition scope, time kind, source, authority, confidence, status and lineage as applicable.

Agents never infer inventory balance, ownership, custody, availability, quality, shipment completion, financial value or legal permission from one movement, scan, document, event or posting reference alone.
Product, lot, serial, handling unit, location, stock position, order, task, shipment, ledger, valuation, document, observation, incident and evidence remain external masters.

Automated agents may append low-risk plans, observations, reconciliations and projections under delegation, but authoritative inventory posting, reversal, protected disclosure and irreversible deletion require explicit external authority.

read: Resolve active Dimension, purpose, role, requested revision, stock-subject scope, assertion kind, status horizon, assurance, freshness, license and access policy; return the minimum permitted projection.
create: Create stable identity, movement class, stock-subject scope, qualified quantity, source-destination transition, source, authority and explicit unknowns before adding execution or posting assertions.
update: Append an immutable plan, execution, posting, exception, reconciliation or correction revision with actor, authority, reason, RFC 3339 effective time and predecessor.
delete: Apply safety, finance, dispute, audit, retention, disposition and legal-hold policy; tombstone eligible Inventory Movement-owned records or withdraw projections while preserving identity, material provenance and non-cascading external references. The adopting Dimension policy owns execution.

checklist.notes: Movement, revision, execution assertion, posting reference, correction, reversal and projection identities remain distinct.
Direction, reason, movement class and planned, physical, observed, posted or reconciled assertion kind are explicit.
Subject scope, quantity, transition, state and event-specific evidence are covered without importing external masters.
Request, physical execution, scan, count, document, posting and resulting balance are independently recognized.
Requested, planned, reserved, released, executing, completed, posted, failed, cancelled, reversed and corrected states preserve history.
Stock subjects, locations, positions, orders, tasks, shipments, postings, documents and evidence use typed references.
Planned, effective, event, observation, record, posting, correction and ingestion clocks remain distinct.
Source and destination site, warehouse, zone, bin, virtual location and read-point functions are explicit.
Sources, actors, methods, observations, postings, derivations, revisions and invalidations are linked.
Inventory ownership, custody, possession, control, responsibility and data mastership are not conflated.
Identity, quantity, unit, transition, clock, role, posting, balance, evidence and crosswalk checks are explicit.
Role, purpose, segregation of duties, commercial sensitivity, minimum projection and audit are represented.
Corrections, reversals, disputes, audit or legal hold, withdrawal and tombstones are explicit and non-cascading.
GS1, UBL, UN/CEFACT, ISA-95, IEC 62264, RFC, PROV, DQV, ODRL and ISO mappings disclose loss.
Registration, classification, binding, planning, evidence, posting reference, correction, reconciliation and projection declare controlled effects.

known_omissions: Industry, warehouse, manufacturing, accounting, valuation, customs, dangerous-goods, safety, privacy, licensing and retention profiles require exact current rules and competent review.
Product, lot, serial, handling unit, location, stock position, order, task, shipment, ledger, document, observation, incident and evidence lifecycles remain in neighboring models.
Certified field crosswalks, balance calculation, costing, allocation algorithms, warehouse execution, autonomous robotics and legal evidence requirements remain future work.
conflicts: Warehouse systems may call a request, task, physical action, scan or ledger posting a movement; the model requires an explicit assertion kind and source profile.
GS1 EPCIS captures visibility events and UBL exchanges fulfilment documents, but neither is assumed to be the universal authoritative inventory ledger.
A physical transfer, ownership transfer, custody transfer, status change, valuation posting and accounting entry may correlate but are different governed facts.
regional_assumptions: UN/CEFACT and UBL are cross-domain exchange sources rather than universal inventory law or warehouse execution policy.
ISA-95 and IEC 62264 are manufacturing integration profiles and do not define all retail, healthcare, customs or field-service movements.
Inventory posting, valuation, tax, title, custody, safety and retention consequences depend on organization, industry and jurisdiction.
adversarial_checks: Reject a movement without stable identity, revision, assertion kind, stock subject, qualified quantity, transition, source, authority and lineage.
Reject a request, reservation, warehouse task, scan, shipment event, inventory balance or accounting entry represented as the movement itself without a discriminator.
Reject physical execution and authoritative inventory posting collapsed into one state or timestamp.
Reject quantity without unit, precision and subject scope or a location transition without source and destination roles.
Reject ownership, custody, availability, quality, financial value or shipment completion inferred from one movement or document alone.
Reject last-write-wins when request, execution, receipt, posting, count or balance assertions conflict; preserve source, clocks, correction and precedence.
Reject authoritative posting, reversal, protected disclosure or record destruction outside delegated external authority.
