boundaryDecision.rationale: The aggregate root is one stock-affecting movement assertion. Request, physical execution, observation, authoritative posting and resulting stock position remain distinguishable and independently sourced.

decisions.rationale: The model owns movement identity, asserted transition, evidence references and correction lineage rather than stock balance or warehouse workflow.
A movement references before-and-after inventory positions, but an event is not automatically contained by the position aggregate.

decisions.concept: Request plan execution observation posting and balance
decisions.rationale: They may occur at different times under different authorities and must not share one status or timestamp.
Product, lot, serial and handling-unit identities remain external while the movement owns the scoped quantity assertion.
Locations, positions, ownership, custody, availability, quality and disposition are independently typed before-and-after references.
Shipment grouping and cross-organizational trace graphs remain external even when they trigger or evidence an inventory movement.
Vercy records posting identity, authority, time and result reference but does not mutate an inventory or accounting ledger.
Prior assertions remain immutable and resolvable; correction or reversal creates a linked successor or compensating record.

decisions.concept: GS1 UBL UN/CEFACT and ISA-95 projections
decisions.rationale: The sources cover different visibility, fulfilment, inventory-report and manufacturing-integration views and none is universal ledger authority.

decisions.concept: Single-provider waiver and local no-tools audit
decisions.rationale: One bounded Claude Sonnet and one bounded Grok attempt each timed out after 120 seconds. Codex separately audited the frozen validated result and comparison without acquiring new facts, so assurance remains reviewable-draft.

publicationHolds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok attempt for WM-FLW-012 each timed out after 120 seconds; no external result was admitted.
Relation hold: WM-OBJ-020 remains a required typed reference rather than an approved parent until joint boundary review.

Boundary hold: product, lot, serial, handling unit, location, stock position, order, task, shipment, trace, ledger, valuation, accounting, document, observation, incident and evidence remain external masters.
Assertion-kind hold: request, plan, reservation, physical execution, observation, posting, balance, correction and reconciliation must remain distinguishable.
Authority hold: authoritative posting, reversal and resulting balance require the external inventory master or ledger authority.
Terminology hold: movement, transfer, transaction, issue, receipt, adjustment, task and posting are profile-specific terms.
Profile hold: warehouse, manufacturing, retail, healthcare, customs, dangerous-goods, safety, accounting, valuation, privacy, licensing and retention profiles need independent validation.
Evidence hold: one scan, count, document, shipment event or posting reference does not alone prove balance, ownership, custody, availability, quality or financial value.
Interoperability hold: all GS1, UBL, UN/CEFACT, ISA-95, IEC 62264, unit, provenance and quality projections require exact release pins, conformance tests and semantic-loss declarations.
Completeness hold: the 24-source draft is broad but does not claim universal industry, legal, operational or accounting coverage.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.

model.name: Supply-chain Trace / Chain of Custody
model.purpose: Provide a reusable governed pattern for linking traceable objects, events, custody assertions, transformations, locations, parties and evidence into a federated time-aware trace graph with qualified queries, gaps and corrections.
model.scope_statement: Owns trace scope, semantic kind and graph revision; trace objective, range, direction and chain-of-custody profile; typed bindings to objects, events, parties, places, movements and evidence; aggregation, transformation and custody edges; qualified clocks, sources, proof and quality; gaps, duplicates, conflicts, error declarations and successors; backward, forward, path and exposure query results; federation, access, retention and loss-aware projections. Products, lots, serials, handling units, shipments, inventory movements, journeys, locations, parties, generic events, observations, custody handovers, documents, credentials, incidents, recall actions, claims and evidence masters remain external.
in_scope: Trace scope, graph and result identity, objective, range, direction, semantic kind, revision and successor lineage
Typed object-event graph, aggregation, transformation, location, party, custody, clock, source, evidence, proof, quality, gap and conflict assertions
Backward and forward query, exposure analysis, federation, privacy, access, retention, audit and interoperability
out_of_scope: Owning product, lot, serial, handling unit, shipment, movement, journey, place, party, event, observation, handover, document, credential, incident, recall action, claim or evidence lifecycles

Equating traceability with tracking, custody with ownership, aggregation with transformation, event assertion with verified fact, physical flow with mass balance or book-and-claim, or exposure result with recall decision
Executing physical custody, product certification, identity issuance, evidence storage, recall, enforcement, protected disclosure or irreversible deletion

boundary_notes.distinction: Goods Movement owns physical logistics flow. Trace / Chain of Custody links source-qualified histories across movements and organizations; the candidate parent signal remains under review.

The trace pattern composes typed event references and graph edges. Generic event identity, occurrence semantics and lifecycle remain external; the candidate COMPOSE relation is accepted only in that limited sense.
Shipment / Consignment owns commercial or transport grouping and status assertions. The trace graph references it as an object and event context without importing that lifecycle.
Inventory Movement owns one stock-affecting transition and external posting reference. The trace graph links movements across organizations but does not calculate stock positions or post ledgers.
The pattern links custody intervals, transfers, acceptance and refusal assertions. The handover event and legal ownership remain independently mastered and must not be inferred from location alone.

Artifacts, digests, signatures, credentials and verification results are references that support assertions. Their issuance, storage, cryptographic validity, certification scope and legal effect remain external.
The pattern may derive a qualified affected set with gaps and uncertainty. Accountable domain authorities own recall, alert, enforcement, remedy and public-disclosure decisions.

Publish trace-object, event-type, business-step, disposition, location, custody-role, quality, access, retention and interoperability registries.
Pin chain-of-custody model, sector, jurisdiction, claim, certification, security, privacy, licensing and exchange profiles.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint trace-scope, graph-revision, edge, gap, contested-set, query-result, exposure-set and projection identifiers only in the adopting Dimension namespace; preserve external master identities as typed references.
registry_links: Dimension-local trace, event, custody-role, classifier, source, access, retention and provenance registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by registry ID, model version, trace scope, mandatory semantic kind, authoritative source IDs, immutable graph revision, query basis and source profile; never use date, lot code, barcode, party, location, document or hash alone as identity.

Keep trace graph, query, result, snapshot, custody claim, object, event, aggregation, transformation, handover, evidence, exposure analysis and recall decision distinct and preserve corrections and successors.
patch_rules: Additive extensions use a Dimension-owned namespace and declare target node, chain-of-custody or sector profile, authority, source, rationale, access, time and interoperability impact.
Breaking changes require a new version, migration and crosswalk maps, compatibility declaration and continued resolution of prior graph revisions, query results and identifiers.
compatibility_rules: Consumers may ignore unknown additive fields only when trace identity, semantic kind, object and event scope, edge meaning, clocks, authority, provenance and access remain intact.
GS1, UN/CEFACT, ISO, FDA, EU, DCSA, IATA and provenance mappings pin source and target versions and declare transformed, omitted or non-round-trippable values.

identity_priority: Authoritative traceability master-system identifier and immutable revision.
Governed globally resolvable trace, edge, query-result or exposure-set IRI.
Adopting-Dimension UUID or ULID when no authoritative external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record timestamps in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z; keep event, effective, observation, record, ingestion, publication and correction times distinct.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Name serial artifacts as {trace-id}--{artifact-kind}--{revision-or-event-id}; never use a date, lot code, barcode, party, location, filename or hash alone as identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, canonicalization profile, media type, byte length, issuer, source and vocabulary versions, graph scope, event and record times, provenance, verification, assurance, license and access marking for each retained artifact.

policies: The adopting Dimension declares who may register scope, bind objects, append events, assert custody, attach proofs, correct, query, derive exposure sets, disclose, retain and tombstone trace records.
Every assertion requires trace and graph revision, semantic kind, subject and edge scope, source, authority, clocks, confidence, quality, access and lineage as applicable.

Agents never infer ownership, custody, product characteristic, safety, compliance, authenticity, recall scope or legal responsibility from location, event, document, digest, signature or credential alone.
Objects, events, movements, parties, places, handovers, observations, documents, credentials, claims, recall actions and evidence remain external masters.

Automated agents may append low-risk source-qualified edges, gap reports, queries and projections under delegation, but custody acceptance, certification, recall, enforcement, protected disclosure and irreversible deletion require accountable external authority.

read: Resolve active Dimension, purpose, role, trace scope and revision, object and time horizon, source freshness, quality, assurance, license and access policy; return the minimum permitted graph projection.
create: Create stable trace scope, semantic kind, objective, object range, direction, source authorities, chain-of-custody profile and explicit unknowns before adding graph edges.
update: Append an immutable object binding, event edge, custody assertion, proof, gap, conflict or correction with actor, authority, reason, RFC 3339 clocks and predecessor.
delete: Apply safety, certification, regulatory, dispute, audit, retention, disposition and legal-hold policy; tombstone eligible Trace-owned records or withdraw projections while preserving identity, material provenance and non-cascading external references. The adopting Dimension policy owns execution.

access.default_rule: Deny mutation and sensitive disclosure unless active Dimension, role, purpose, commercial confidentiality, location, personal data, security, license and field policy grant the action; expose the minimum necessary graph slice.
exceptions: Emergency or regulatory access must be legally grounded, time-limited, purpose-bound, attributable, independently reviewed and unable to erase immutable trace, conflict, correction or legal-hold evidence.
audit_requirements: Log actor, role, purpose, trace and revision identity, query or action, decision, policy and vocabulary versions, RFC 3339 timestamp with offset, affected graph scope, source evidence and outcome for privileged mutation or disclosure.

read_order: Read the nearest Dimension-owner AGENTS.md, trace and source authorities, active custody model, sector, jurisdiction, time, access, retention, licensing and disclosure policies.
Read this model AGENTS.md, pinned spec.yaml and required object, event, movement, party, place, handover, document, credential, recall, claim and evidence instructions before mutation.

coverage.claim: WM-FLW-013 covers a reusable Supply-chain Trace / Chain of Custody pattern with graph and result identity, trace objective, object-event composition, aggregation, transformation, location, parties, custody, clocks, evidence, integrity, quality, correction, backward and forward query, exposure analysis, federation, governance and loss-aware interoperability. Sector, jurisdiction, certification, claims, implementation-conformance and independent-review questions remain deferred.

checklist.notes: Trace scope, graph revision, query request, result, snapshot, claim, edge and exposure-set identities remain distinct.
Trace objective, direction, coverage and chain-of-custody profile are mandatory and versioned.
Graph scope, edge semantics, gaps, conflicts and query basis are covered without importing external masters.
Authoritative identity, physical observation, business assertion, document, signature and verification result are distinguished.
Registration, append, validation, contest, correction, supersession, withdrawal, retention and tombstone preserve history.
Objects, events, aggregation, transformation, locations, parties, movements, handovers, documents and decisions use typed edges.
Event, effective, observation, record, ingestion, publication and correction clocks remain distinct.
Read point, business location, source, destination, facility and jurisdiction functions are explicit.
Sources, agents, methods, delegations, evidence, derivations, revisions and invalidations are linked.
Ownership, custody, possession, control, responsibility and data mastership are not conflated.
Identity, edge, clock, composition, transformation, custody, proof, quality, path and crosswalk checks are explicit.
Role, purpose, confidentiality, personal data, location sensitivity, minimum graph projection and audit are represented.
Corrections, contested sets, recall or legal hold, withdrawal and tombstones are explicit and non-cascading.
GS1, UN/CEFACT, ISO, FDA, EU, DCSA, IATA, RFC, PROV, DQV, ODRL and Data Integrity mappings disclose loss.
Scope registration, object and event linking, custody assertion, proof, correction, query, exposure and projection declare controlled effects.

known_omissions: Sector, jurisdiction, chain-of-custody claim, certification, customs, dangerous-goods, safety, privacy, security, licensing and retention profiles require exact current rules and competent review.
Objects, events, movements, parties, places, handovers, observations, documents, credentials, claims, recall actions and evidence lifecycles remain in neighboring models.

Certified field crosswalks, identity resolution, graph completeness metrics, secure federation, signature suites, exposure algorithms, recall decision rules and legal evidence requirements remain future work.
conflicts: Traceability covers product history and relationship paths, tracking often emphasizes current location or status, and chain of custody governs characteristic attribution; the model requires an explicit semantic kind and profile.
Physical segregation, controlled blending, mass balance and book-and-claim permit different relationships between physical material and attributed characteristics and cannot share one inference rule.
An event assertion, document, digest, signature, credential and successful verification establish different properties and do not by themselves prove real-world truth, custody or product conformity.
regional_assumptions: FDA food traceability and EU Digital Product Passport are jurisdictional and product-scope profiles rather than universal supply-chain rules.
DCSA and IATA are maritime-container and air-cargo modal profiles and do not define all transport or custody contexts.
Recall, certification, title, custody, privacy, security, retention and evidential consequences depend on sector, contract and jurisdiction.
adversarial_checks: Reject a trace without stable scope identity, semantic kind, revision, object and event range, graph basis, source authority and lineage.
Reject traceability, tracking, chain of custody, provenance, audit log, shipment history and distributed software trace treated as universal aliases.
Reject custody inferred from location, ownership inferred from custody, conformity inferred from a signature or recall inferred from an exposure result.
Reject aggregation and transformation collapsed into one relationship or membership represented without a validity interval and source.
Reject event, observation, record, ingestion and correction times collapsed into one timestamp.
Reject last-write-wins when sources conflict; preserve competing assertions, gaps, evidence, correction and precedence policy.
Reject protected graph disclosure, certification, recall, enforcement or record destruction outside delegated authority.

providerPolicy.scope: Canonical single-stream subject-model research after the six-workstream consolidation

waived_providers.reason: Claude produced no result on prior 1800-second and 900-second attempts and again timed out on bounded 600-second Sonnet and 300-second Haiku passes. The owner prioritized completion over provider availability.

The repository owner authorized completion without Grok when Grok is unavailable, slow or schema-invalid. Grok may still be attempted as a bounded supplemental reviewer, but its failure never blocks a valid Claude plus no-tools result.

providerPolicy.review_rule: Codex may complete source-grounded fallback research after bounded Claude and Grok attempts fail. It requires a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remains reviewable-draft with a visible absence-of-external-review hold.

supplemental_provider_attempts.admission_rule: Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.
Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.

boundaryDecision.rationale: The root is a reusable cross-organizational graph and query pattern. It links externally mastered objects, events and evidence while preserving source authority, gaps and corrections.

decisions.rationale: The pattern owns graph scope, typed edges, query results, gaps and correction lineage rather than the lifecycle of linked records.

decisions.concept: Persistent graph query result snapshot and claim
decisions.rationale: A query and its qualified result do not replace the underlying graph, and a chain-of-custody claim has additional attribution rules.
Goods Movement is a broader physical-flow context, while the trace pattern also covers custody claims and federated evidence.
The trace graph composes event references and edges but generic event identity and lifecycle remain external.
Parent-child membership changes and input-output process changes have different semantics and evidence.

decisions.concept: Custody possession control responsibility and ownership
decisions.rationale: Neither location nor custody alone establishes ownership or legal responsibility.

decisions.concept: Physical segregation controlled blending mass balance and book-and-claim
decisions.rationale: The profiles permit different links between physical material flow and attributed product characteristics.

decisions.concept: Evidence digest signature credential and verification
decisions.rationale: Integrity or successful verification can establish document properties while the real-world assertion and authority still require evaluation.
The pattern derives a qualified affected set and uncertainty; accountable external authorities own recall, alert and enforcement decisions.

decisions.concept: Single-provider waiver and local no-tools audit
decisions.rationale: One bounded Claude Sonnet and one bounded Grok attempt each timed out after 120 seconds. Codex separately audited the frozen validated result and comparison without acquiring new facts, so assurance remains reviewable-draft.

publicationHolds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok attempt for WM-FLW-013 each timed out after 120 seconds; no external result was admitted.
Relation hold: WM-FLW-004 remains a compositional reference rather than an approved parent until joint boundary review.
Composition hold: WM-ACT-015 is composed only as typed event references; generic event identity and lifecycle remain external.

Boundary hold: products, lots, serials, handling units, shipments, movements, journeys, places, parties, events, observations, handovers, documents, credentials, incidents, recalls, claims and evidence remain external masters.
Claim-model hold: physical segregation, controlled blending, mass balance and book-and-claim require explicit profile and attribution rules.
Truth hold: an event, location, document, digest, signature, credential or verification result does not alone prove custody, ownership, conformity, safety or legal responsibility.
Decision hold: exposure results require an accountable external authority for recall, certification, enforcement, remedy or public disclosure.
Profile hold: food, pharmaceuticals, mining, forestry, energy, circularity, maritime, air cargo, customs, dangerous-goods and jurisdiction profiles need independent validation.
Interoperability hold: GS1, UN/CEFACT, ISO, FDA, EU, DCSA, IATA, RFC and W3C projections require exact release pins, conformance tests and semantic-loss declarations.
Completeness hold: the 24-source draft is broad but does not claim universal sector, legal, evidential or operational coverage.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.

model.name: Work Order
model.purpose: Represent an authoritative, versioned instruction that authorizes and constrains one or more units of work while preserving boundaries to requests, procedures, schedules and performed-work evidence.
model.scope_statement: Owns order identity, authorization, scope, requirements, administrative lifecycle, change control, acceptance criteria and closure disposition; references execution and domain records governed elsewhere.
in_scope: Order identity, class, authority, scope, requirements, constraints and order-level planning commitments
Administrative state transitions, revisions, cancellation, acceptance decision, closure and governance metadata
Typed references to tasks, procedures, targets, resources, contracts, schedules and performed-work evidence
out_of_scope: Task execution semantics, detailed scheduling, inventory transactions, cost accounting, access enforcement and proof that physical work occurred
Lifecycle ownership of referenced assets, people, organizations, locations, contracts, procedures or evidence records

boundary_notes.distinction: A request proposes or demands work and can be rejected; a work order is an authorized instruction with controlled scope and lifecycle.
The order may contain task references and pin procedure versions, but task execution semantics and reusable instructions remain in their own models.
A work order authorizes work; performed-work records and evidence establish what actually happened and are only referenced here.
The order may carry windows and commitments, but resource-level sequencing and calendar optimization belong to a schedule model.

functions.name: Create draft order
functions.description: Establish a proposed order identity, origin and scope without granting authority.
preconditions: request or authorized drafting purpose exists
effects: a traceable but non-authorized order draft exists

functions.name: Validate order boundary
functions.description: Check required order facts, external references and separation from request, procedure and execution records.
preconditions: order revision is resolvable
effects: boundary, reference and semantic failures are recorded

functions.name: Authorize order
functions.description: Issue an immutable revision under a verified authority and effective scope.
preconditions: validation passed
issuer authority is current
effects: authorization event and immutable issued meaning are recorded

functions.name: Release order
functions.description: Expose an authorized revision to its declared dispatch or execution context.
preconditions: order is authorized
release constraints are satisfied
effects: order becomes available to the declared execution context

functions.name: Revise order
functions.description: Create a traceable successor without overwriting an issued revision.
preconditions: change authority is valid
effects: old and new meaning remain reconstructable

functions.name: Suspend or resume order
functions.description: Temporarily inhibit or restore administrative availability under named authority and reason.
preconditions: transition is allowed
authority is valid
effects: administrative availability changes without erasing history

functions.name: Cancel order
functions.description: Withdraw remaining authorization while preserving evidence and residual obligations.
preconditions: cancellation policy permits the transition
effects: future authorization ends and historical references remain resolvable

functions.name: Record completion claim
functions.description: Bind external performed-work evidence without silently asserting acceptance.
preconditions: external evidence is resolvable
effects: completion claim becomes reviewable separately from order state

functions.name: Accept or reject result
functions.description: Evaluate referenced evidence against the issued acceptance criteria and record the authorized decision.
preconditions: criteria and verifier authority are explicit
effects: accepted, rejected or conditional disposition is recorded

functions.name: Close order
functions.description: Finalize disposition, unresolved exceptions and retention metadata after an authorized decision.
preconditions: closure prerequisites are satisfied
effects: order is closed but its identity, history and references remain governed

composition.purpose: Groups typed task references and order-local parameters without claiming ownership of task execution semantics.
Pins the executable instruction version while keeping reusable procedure content outside the order.
Delegates detailed sequencing and capacity allocation while retaining order-level timing commitments.

composition.purpose: Uses authoritative domain identities without copying their properties or lifecycles.

Separates authorization from claims and proof of actual execution.

composition.target: ISA-95, OPC UA ISA-95, PLCS and UN/EDIFACT concepts

owner_package_requirements: Declare the Dimension owner, accountable stewards and authority delegation chain.
Declare the Dimension namespace, identity master systems and authoritative work-order repository.
Publish registries for models, objects, events and relation types plus applicable retention and access policies.

dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint identifiers only inside the adopting Dimension's governed namespace; preserve upstream master-system identifiers and aliases without silently re-keying them.
registry_links: Dimension-local model, object and event registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by registry ID, model version, stable node IDs and explicit value units; never infer execution from administrative order state.
Issued revisions are immutable and superseded by linked successors rather than overwritten.
patch_rules: Additive extensions use a Dimension-owned namespace and declare their target bundle, layer, finding or artifact plus source and rationale.
Breaking changes require a new model version, migration mapping, compatibility declaration and preserved access to prior versions.
compatibility_rules: Consumers ignore unknown additive fields only when required semantics and access controls remain intact.
Mappings to external job or work-order schemas must declare lossy fields, code-list versions and timezone handling.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system work-order identifier and immutable issued-revision identifier.
Governed globally resolvable IRI or federation identifier.
Adopting-Dimension UUID or ULID when no authoritative external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record event timestamps in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z; keep event, effective, observation and ingestion times distinct.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Name serial artifacts as {order-id}--{artifact-kind}--{revision-or-event-id}; never use a date alone as identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store a cryptographic digest, media type, byte length, issuer, provenance and immutable version reference for every retained serial artifact.

policies: The adopting Dimension defines who may draft, authorize, release, revise, cancel, accept and close each order class.
Facts, hypotheses and unknown values remain explicitly distinct and carry source, observation time and confidence where applicable.
Safety, privacy, commercial confidentiality, export control and legal-hold policies are evaluated before disclosure or mutation.
External references are resolved by pinned identity and version, with stale, missing or lossy bindings reported rather than guessed.

read: Resolve the model version, owner policy and referenced master systems; apply field- and artifact-level access rules and record material reads where policy requires.
create: Create a draft only under an authorized purpose, allocate identity by priority, validate required boundary facts and keep it non-executable until an authorization event.
update: Create an immutable successor revision for issued meaning, record actor, authority, reason and effective time, and validate references and transitions before and after the change.
delete: Apply retention, legal-hold and deletion policy; tombstone issued orders or use approved cryptographic erasure while preserving minimum identity and non-cascading reference integrity.

boundaryDecision.rationale: The record-plane label standalone-mm does not determine the subject kind. Work Order is defensibly an aggregate because one authoritative root governs authorization, scope, requirements, state, revisions, acceptance criteria and closure while composing or referencing subordinate records.

decisions.rationale: The model consistently treats a request as an input that can be rejected and the order as an authorized instruction, matching the cited PLCS distinction and preventing demand records from becoming executable by implication.

Administrative release, dispatch and closure never prove that work occurred; completion and performance records remain external evidence references, which is essential for auditability and safe agent behavior.

The order can compose typed task references and order-local parameters without owning task execution semantics. The candidate WM-ACT-006 relation remains visible for later cross-model cardinality and lifecycle review.

A Work Order is an abstract governed record, so mass, material, geometry and other physical properties must belong to referenced targets and resources rather than being fabricated on the order itself.

The draft captures lifecycle semantics and transition authority but intentionally avoids one universal code list because ISA-95, OPC UA, PLCS and operational implementations use different state names and granularities.

Immutable issued revisions, linked successors, retention review, legal holds and tombstones preserve historical meaning and prevent destructive updates from invalidating external evidence or references.
Master-system identity is prioritized, date-only naming is forbidden, and RFC 3339 timestamps require seconds and explicit offsets while separating event, effective, observation and ingestion times.

The structure uses concepts supported by ISA, OPC Foundation, OASIS PLCS and UNECE, but exact implementation mappings and code-list versions remain explicit profile work rather than unsupported conformance claims.
Default-deny mutation and disclosure, granular scopes, purpose-bound emergency access and attributable audit records give agents actionable controls without embedding a separate enforcement engine.

All findings expose at least value, authority/provenance and validation/change questions across broad semantic kinds. Their systematic wording is useful for machine completion but still warrants later domain-profile editorial review.
